date_note: The page gives no earlier day than its publication day, 24 November.
title: Austrian police warn of phishing messages with real booking details, linked to suspected tourism data leaks
geo_basis: country: the article reports a police warning for people in Austria
summary: Heute.at reports that Austrian police are receiving more complaints about phishing emails, SMS and WhatsApp messages that contain correct booking details. According to the article, the data probably comes from recent suspected data breaches at tourism associations and hotel chains. The links lead to fake websites that try to capture payment and login data.
plain: Police in Austria say convincing fake messages with real booking details are increasing. The article says the data probably comes from suspected hotel and tourism data leaks.
exec: Heute.at reports police warnings about phishing built on real booking data, which the article links to suspected tourism and hotel data breaches.
action: Austrian police advise: do not open links in suspicious messages, contact the hotel or tourism association through known official contacts, and if data was shared, call your bank at once to block cards and report it to police.

validation.note: Only Heute.at was read; the police's own page was not read. The link to tourism data breaches is the article's suspicion, not confirmed.

review.note: summary, hedged leak link, date, advice vs Heute.at
